races.name: Summer Saturday Series At Doncaster Racecourse Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: The Ubermensch
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs strong pace, 18 days off ideal preparation, finished well at Wolverhampton last time
runners_data.comment: 0-7 but he still has potential and looks interesting at this new trip; cheekpieces added
runners_data.spotlight: 0-7 but he's finished runner-up in two of his four handicaps and he kept on well when fourth at Wolverhampton (9.4f, AW) last month; looks worth a try at this new trip and he's in the mix with cheekpieces added.

runners_data.name: It's Only Fun
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits race shape, back up 4lb after recent Southwell win but cheekpieces back on
runners_data.comment: Cashed in on a reduced mark when scoring at Southwell (1m3f) last month; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Took advantage of a reduced mark when battling well to score at 20-1 at Southwell (1m3f, AW; cheekpieces reapplied) two weeks ago; back up 4lb in the weights but he remains well treated on old form and his first win was on turf; shortlisted.

runners_data.name: Animato
runners_data.note: Only front-runner in field, 314 days off is major concern despite past class over this trip
runners_data.comment: His last win was over 2m in May 2024; has work to do back on the Flat after a break
runners_data.spotlight: Five-time Flat winner but last two were over 2m at Catterick in May 2024; well handicapped on old form but has mixed record since switched to hurdling in his last seven starts; returns after a break but his tactical speed will be tested back in this sphere and others are preferred.

runners_data.name: Sweet Kiss
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with tactical speed, good recent fourth suggests return to form, strong claimer takes 5lb off
runners_data.spotlight: Won three times under Jake Dickson last August/September (1m2f, good to firm-good to soft); no impact in two runs this season but she caught the eye with her late headway at Carlisle (1m3f, good) last Friday; has claims if she can build on that and she won't mind what the weather does.

runners_data.name: Division Day
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from 244-day break after hurdling, only 1lb higher than last Flat win
runners_data.comment: Runner-up over hurdles in last two starts and he needs a close look back on the Flat
runners_data.spotlight: Dual 1m6f Flat winner who has finished runner-up in novice/maiden hurdles (2m/2m4f) in his last two runs; returns after four months off but he's only 1lb higher than for his last win and it would be a positive if the forecast rain arrives; needs a close look back on the Flat.

runners_data.name: Letmeseethecolts
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who can track Animato, struggled in last two since Pontefract win but retains ability
runners_data.comment: Easy win at Pontefract last April but she's been out of sorts in both subsequent runs
runners_data.spotlight: Hit a personal best with her clearcut win at Pontefract (1m4f, good) last April but she's had only two runs since and has struggled in both of them; has some questions to answer and she needs a major revival back up in trip.

runners_data.name: Muhib
runners_data.note: Hold-up style on lowest weight, consistent spring form including Catterick third, Warren Fentiman 7lb claim helps
runners_data.comment: Some good efforts this spring but he was well held last time and is now 0-23
runners_data.spotlight: Some creditable efforts this spring including when third at Catterick (1m4f, good) last month; hard to rule out another good run but he didn't really fire at Pontefract last time and his overall record is now 0-23.

races.paceDynamic: Animato will take this field along from the front with Letmeseethecolts likely to track him in second, creating a measured gallop over this staying trip. The majority of the field - The Ubermensch, It's Only Fun, Sweet Kiss, Division Day and Muhib - are all hold-up horses who will be relying on a finishing kick. With only one confirmed front-runner and five hold-up performers, this sets up perfectly for the closers who should get a strong pace to aim at and plenty of cover before unleashing late runs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Favours Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Animato and Letmeseethecolts set a genuine pace from flag to finish
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get the ideal setup with a true test of stamina and can time their runs perfectly in the straight. The sustained gallop plays to the strengths of the back-markers who have shown their best form when getting a strong pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Animato gets an easy lead and Letmeseethecolts doesn't apply pressure
scenarios.body: The front two get away with soft fractions and have too much left in the tank for the closers to peg back. Animato's class on old form and Letmeseethecolts' turn of foot become decisive factors.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Suits Versatile
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop becomes steady but honest throughout the middle stages
scenarios.body: Neither the front-runners nor pure hold-up horses get their optimal conditions, favouring those with tactical speed. Horses who can adapt their running style and quicken off a steady pace hold the edge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Goes Wrong
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses go too fast early or the hold-up horses get blocked
scenarios.body: Poor positioning or traffic problems leave several fancied runners with too much to do. The race becomes a lottery with an outsider potentially capitalizing on the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Animato's fitness after 314 days off and recent hurdling campaign - if he stops quickly the race shape changes completely
Traffic problems for the five hold-up horses if they all get covered up turning for home with limited pace-setters ahead
Letmeseethecolts' willingness to race prominently - if he drops back to midfield the pace could become crawling
Division Day's sharpness returning from four months off hurdling back to this Flat trip
The Ubermensch and It's Only Fun both need the sustained gallop this small field with one leader should provide

races.name: Support Weston Park Cancer Charity Today Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B-D) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: My Mate Roger
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with consistent placed form who should benefit from the strong early pace and suits this distance after near-miss at Windsor
runners_data.comment: Runner-up in all three starts and sets useful standard on his close call at Windsor latest
runners_data.spotlight: 75,000euros breeze-up 2yo; finished runner-up in his three starts since December including a near-miss when upped to 1m2f at Windsor (good to firm) last month; sets useful standard on that form and his RPRs have been progressive so far; strong contender.

runners_data.name: Hawksworth
runners_data.note: Debutant from high-class family but Quinn stable in poor form and faces experienced rivals on first start
runners_data.comment: 23,000euros yearling; already been gelded and this looks a tough starting point
runners_data.spotlight: 23,000euros yearling; first foal; dam placed 7f-8.6f 2yo (RPR 79), out of unraced sister to Group-placed 1m4f winner Sayida, half-sister to Derby winner Masar; already been gelded and this looks a tough starting point.

runners_data.name: Ingemar
runners_data.note: Well-bred newcomer from powerful Meehan yard but limited stable runners recently and needs to show ability immediately
runners_data.comment: 42,000euros yearling; has good target to aim at on debut and market should guide
runners_data.spotlight: 42,000euros yearling; ninth foal; gelded half-brother to 1m Group 3 winner Indian Blessing and two useful French midde-distance winners; dam useful 1m2f/1m4f winner; has good target to aim at on debut and market should guide.

runners_data.name: Le Morbihan
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner from excellent family who will set honest pace but may find sustained battle difficult
runners_data.comment: Showed promise on Beverley debut and he should benefit from that experience
runners_data.spotlight: 65,000euros yearling; dam unraced sister to 7f/8.6f 2yo winner Pomelo, half-sister to Group 1 scorers Bluestocking (1m2f/1m4f including Arc) and Qirat (1m Sussex Stakes); 22-1 at Beverley (1m2f, good) in April but he ran well for a long way and was beaten only about 4l in fourth of eight; this is a tougher assignment but that was an encouraging start and he should benefit from the experience.

runners_data.name: Harmonics
runners_data.note: Hold-up type in good current form after Southwell win who should appreciate the step up in distance
runners_data.comment: Won at Southwell last month and he's open to more progress upped in trip; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Made a low-key start at Southwell (1m, AW) in April but he left that form well behind when beating 11 rivals on his return visit (7-2) two weeks ago; this is tougher under a penalty but he has a useful pedigree and is open to more progress on this step up in trip; respected.

runners_data.name: I Got Rhythm
runners_data.note: Held-up performer who was well beaten on debut but represents stable that can improve horses significantly
runners_data.comment: 80-1 and was always in rear throughout on his Newmarket debut (1m, good) last month
runners_data.spotlight: 80-1 and was always in rear throughout on his Newmarket debut (1m, good) last month; was beaten around 16l in that race and he's probably a longer-term prospect.

runners_data.name: West Sleekburn Lad
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from long layoff with poor previous form and looks outclassed in this company
runners_data.comment: 66-1 and he failed to beat a rival on Catterick debut in October; best watched on return
runners_data.spotlight: Missed the break and was always behind when last of ten on his Catterick debut (7f, good; 66-1) in October; best watched on return.

runners_data.name: Cliff Danger
runners_data.note: Front-running type who shaped with promise last time but may struggle to sustain battle with Le Morbihan throughout
runners_data.comment: Showed promise over 1m2f at Nottingham and has each-way claims if he can build on that
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't show a great deal on Wetherby debut (1m) in April but, after a gelding operation, he shaped with promise when fourth at Nottingham (1m2f, good to soft) last month; has each-way claims if he can take another step forward and he's in the mix.

runners_data.name: Annahita
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with modest form but carries headgear and represents stable in decent current form
runners_data.comment: Down the field in both runs and handicaps look the way forward after this
runners_data.spotlight: Modest form when down the field at Kempton (1m, AW) in October and she was beaten 16l on her Lingfield reappearance (11-2) last month; still early days but she has a lot to find here and handicaps will be more suitable.

races.paceDynamic: Le Morbihan and Cliff Danger will set the early fractions with both confirmed front-runners likely to contest the lead through the first half of this 1m2f contest. The honest gallop they establish should create a solid test of stamina, particularly with good to firm ground encouraging a true pace. The sustained nature of their duel will set up the race perfectly for hold-up horses to close late. This race shape strongly favours hold-up performers who can finish with one sustained run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Profit
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners maintain their duel into the straight
scenarios.body: The sustained pace will take its toll on Le Morbihan and Cliff Danger, creating perfect conditions for closers to sweep past in the final furlong. My Mate Roger and Harmonics are ideally positioned to capitalize with their proven finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of Le Morbihan or Cliff Danger gets loose early
scenarios.body: A clear leader could dictate terms and have enough left to resist the late challenge, particularly if they can steal a march at the top of the straight. Le Morbihan's superior breeding suggests he's more likely to sustain his effort.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutant Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If either Hawksworth or Ingemar shows significant improvement
scenarios.body: The lightly-raced types could have enough natural ability to overcome their inexperience, benefiting from the strong pace up front. Their superior breeding and stable connections suggest untapped potential that could be unleashed here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners fail to maintain their battle
scenarios.body: A moderate early pace would turn this into more of a sprint finish, potentially suiting any horse with natural speed regardless of preferred running style. This scenario makes the race far more open but seems unlikely given both leaders' confirmed front-running tendencies.

watchPoints.text: Le Morbihan and Cliff Danger establishing a genuine battle from the outset as anything less than honest pace completely changes the race dynamics
My Mate Roger getting a clear run in the straight as he's shown consistent placed form and needs racing room to deliver his finishing kick
Hawksworth showing early pace or tactical speed as any market confidence would suggest connections expect a bold debut performance
The going reports showing good to firm throughout the card as any change to softer conditions would impact several runners' chances
Harmonics settling kindly in rear given his recent all-weather win suggests he's in good current form

races.name: Hits Radio Proudly Supports WPCC Novice Stakes Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Master Of Delphi
runners_data.note: Unknown racing style but expensive breeding suggests quality, though lightly raced status makes him hard to assess tactically
runners_data.comment: 150,000euros breeze-up 2yo; has useful standard to aim at on debut and market should guide
runners_data.spotlight: $100,000 yearling, 150,000euros breeze-up 2yo; seventh foal; gelded half-brother to winners Desert Peace (7f-1m2f AW/dirt including 2yo; RPR 98), Cantata (6.5f 2yo/8.5f dirt) and Mission Beach (5f-6.5f turf/dirt including 2yo); dam US 4.5f dirt 2yo winner (including stakes); this looks a tough starting point but interesting to see how he figures in market.

runners_data.name: Upper East
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's expensive yearling with unknown style but proven trainer's 14-day form suggests preparation confidence
runners_data.comment: 300,000gns yearling; has useful target to aim at on debut but he needs checking in market
runners_data.spotlight: 300,000gns yearling; second foal; dam 5.7f/6f winner (RPR 89), half-sister to smart 1m-1m6f winner Micro Manage and Listed winners Magnanimous (1m), Thornbrook (1m) and Seisai (7.4f 2yo), out of close relative of 1m4f Group 1 winner Mont Ormel; has useful target to aim on debut but he needs watching in market.

runners_data.name: Impierious
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs the pace to develop, 50 days off may need the run but has shown decent form previously
runners_data.comment: Promising third in the Wood Ditton and he should know more this time; in the mix
runners_data.spotlight: Closely related to 1m-1m4f winner Mashhoor (including Group 3; RPR 115) and he's a half-brother to seven winners; beaten 8l when third in the Wood Ditton at Newmarket (1m, good) in April but he looked inexperienced and that was a promising effort behind an impressive winner; should know more this time and he's a likely improver on his second start.

runners_data.name: Forever Endless
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but limited ability shown so far, 80-1 debut suggests he's outclassed at this level
runners_data.comment: 80-1 and he finished a remote fifth of six on Nottingham debut (8.3f, good) last month
runners_data.spotlight: 80-1 and he finished a remote fifth of six on Nottingham debut (8.3f, good) last month; opposable.

runners_data.name: Ruler Of Time
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who will lead throughout, 126 days off is a concern but Appleby's stable form is solid enough
runners_data.spotlight: RPR of 87 when runner-up in three of his four starts including a close second in a big-field handicap at Meydan (1m, good) in January; just about sets the standard on his return and he should have more to offer at this trip; key player.

runners_data.name: Seet
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with promising debut form, the step up to a mile should suit her developing stamina
runners_data.comment: Well-bred filly who won in good style at Wolverhampton last month; respected under penalty
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to five winners including Kalpana (8.6f-1m4f including Group 1; RPR 123); shaped with promise on Newbury debut (7f, good) in April and she found plenty of progress when scoring in good style on the step up to 8.6f at Wolverhampton (100-30) last month; has a penalty back on turf but she looks a smart prospect and is strongly respected.

runners_data.name: Electric Dreams
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse but non-runner status eliminates tactical impact, expensive yearling who has disappointed so far
runners_data.comment: Well held in both runs this spring and this looks a tough assignment
runners_data.spotlight: 475,000gns yearling; didn't live up to market expectations on Kempton debut (1m, AW) in April and was well held again at Newbury (1m2f, good) last month; still early days but this looks a tough assignment and handicaps will be more suitable.

races.paceDynamic: Ruler Of Time is the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate a sustainable pace from the gates, unlikely to be pressured early with most rivals adopting hold-up tactics. The field splits into Ruler Of Time leading, then a gap to the hold-up brigade of Impierious, Forever Endless, Seet and Electric Dreams, with the two unknowns Master Of Delphi and Upper East adding tactical uncertainty. This creates a moderate early pace that will quicken significantly in the final two furlongs as the hold-up horses unleash their finishing kicks. This race shape strongly favours horses with proven finishing speed and tactical pace who can capitalise on the steady early gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Brigade Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If the pace remains steady throughout and Ruler Of Time maintains his lead into the straight without excessive early pressure
scenarios.body: The moderate tempo allows the hold-up horses to conserve energy and produce devastating late kicks, with Seet and Impierious best placed to exploit their superior finishing speed. Ruler Of Time's stamina will be tested by the sustained finishing kicks behind him.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Ruler Of Time faces no serious early pressure and the hold-up horses are caught flat-footed by a quickening pace
scenarios.body: His class advantage and tactical position prove decisive as he maintains a strong gallop when the closers make their moves too late. The moderate early pace suits his racing style perfectly and he has enough in reserve to repel late challenges.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Newcomers Spring Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Master Of Delphi or Upper East possess superior natural ability and benefit from the steady early pace
scenarios.body: Their expensive breeding and connections suggest untapped potential that could be unleashed with proper tactical positioning behind Ruler Of Time. The race setup allows them to learn on the job while having every chance to show their true worth.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Ruler Of Time goes too slow early and the race becomes a sprint from the two-furlong pole
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure creates a messy finish where any horse with a turn of foot can capitalise, potentially favouring those who position closest to the pace. Form becomes less relevant in a slowly-run tactical affair that turns into a dash.

watchPoints.text: Ruler Of Time's fitness after 126 days off - any sign of rustiness early could compromise his front-running tactics
Master Of Delphi and Upper East's market moves pre-race given their unknown ability and expensive breeding backgrounds
How quickly the hold-up horses can organise their challenge if Ruler Of Time sets a crawling pace through the early stages
Seet's positioning in the field given her promising debut and whether De La Sayette can secure a clear run in the straight
The overall tempo through the first half-mile as this will determine whether stamina or speed becomes the decisive factor

races.name: Rotabroach Proudly Supports WPCC Handicap

runners_data.name: King's Cavalry
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with recent 7f good ground form win, carries confidence but faces traffic dangers with other prominent types
runners_data.comment: Easy odds-on win at Leicester and he's an interesting contender on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Kingman colt who made it third-time lucky when landing the odds in good style at Leicester (7f, good to firm) last month; looks on a workable mark now switched to a handicap and this related colt should have more to offer; interesting contender.

runners_data.name: Toastmaster
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type switching yards, ran well at York in similar conditions but still seeking first career win
runners_data.comment: 0-8 but was a close third in big-field handicap at York on recent stable debut; in the mix
runners_data.spotlight: 0-8 but he was consistent for the Crisfords and made a good start for new yard when close third in big-field handicap at York (7f, good) last month; ties in closely with French Affair on that form and he's in the mix.

runners_data.name: Rogue Messiah
runners_data.note: Prominent racer stepping up in trip after 6f wins, unexposed but faces crowded tactical position
runners_data.comment: Record of 2-4 for Jack Jones and he's open to more progress upped to 7f for new yard
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed gelding who won two of his four starts for Jack Jones, including on handicap debut at Lingfield (6f, AW) in April; up 5lb but he's bred to stay this extra furlong and is open to more progress on his first run for James Owen; respected.

runners_data.name: Blakefell
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from wind surgery with recent win, tactical advantage but this is much stronger field
runners_data.comment: Won after wind surgery at Musselburgh but this is tougher on handicap debut; needs more
runners_data.spotlight: Returned after wind surgery with a Musselburgh maiden win (7f, good) two weeks ago, but he didn't need to improve to take that prize; still unexposed but this is a deeper race on handicap debut and others are preferred.

runners_data.name: King's Trust
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with Gosden polish, recent stalls issue concerning and carries headgear suggesting temperament issues
runners_data.comment: Southwell winner but he's blotted his copybook since; needs to raise his game back on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Beat one who is now on a mark of 95 off level weights at Southwell last October (7f); blotted his copybook by playing up before breaking out of the stalls on intended seasonal/handicap debut in 1m contest at Ascot last month; looked more relaxed at Kempton last week but he never got involved from a wide draw; still early days but he needs to raise his game back on turf.

runners_data.name: French Affair
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in good form from York run, faces tactical nightmare with so many wanting same position
runners_data.comment: Record of 1-11 but he went close in a 20-runner handicap at York last time; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Just one win from 11 starts but he hit a personal best when going close in a 20-runner handicap at York (7f, good) last month; the first three pulled clear in that race and he's strongly respected off only 1lb higher.

runners_data.name: Valpovo
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with 223-day absence, French form hard to assess but long layoff major concern
runners_data.comment: Won in France on the second of three 2yo runs; needs close look on handicap/stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Had three runs in France as a 2yo and he won at La Teste De Buch (9.5f, heavy) on his second start; changed hands for 40,000gns in October; returns after 223 days off but he has a striking pedigree and needs watching in market on handicap/stable debut.

runners_data.name: Illy's Roo
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who won over 7f but recent form poor, headgear suggests connections trying everything
runners_data.comment: Three wins at 7f but he's been well held in last three runs and is exposed after 12 starts
runners_data.spotlight: All three wins have come over 7f and latest was at Southwell in March; only 2lb higher than for that win but he's finished down the field in last three runs and he's the most exposed runner in this line-up; passed over.

runners_data.name: Thunder Call
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with Haggas/Marquand team, well-bred with tactical advantage in this race shape
runners_data.comment: Easy win in Kempton maiden (6f) last month and he's a big player again on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Well-bred colt who is closely related to 7f 2yo/1m Group 3 winner Skardu (RPR 114); left his initial form well behind when runner-up here (6f, heavy) in November and he found more improvement with an emphatic win on his Kempton reappearance (6f, AW) last month; now goes back up in trip but he looks a useful prospect and is a big player for in-form yard.

runners_data.name: Sanaam
runners_data.note: Only front-runner gives tactical edge, disappointed last time but race shape strongly in his favour
runners_data.comment: Disappointing on handicap debut at Wetherby and his standout form was on sole AW start
runners_data.spotlight: Forged clear in a Southwell maiden (7f, Tapeta) towards the end of last year but he was disappointing on handicap debut at Wetherby (7f, good to firm; 4-1) in April; has bit to prove again after that 8l defeat and his standout form was on his sole AW run.

runners_data.name: Night Patrol
runners_data.note: Prominent type with shock Newbury win, inconsistent since but could benefit if pace collapses
runners_data.comment: 125-1 winner at Newbury last September but he's not gone on from that in two runs since
runners_data.spotlight: Won a Newbury novice (7f, good to soft) for Richard Hannon last September but that was a shock at 125-1 and he's not gone on from that in two handicaps since; still lightly raced but he was out the back on recent stable debut at Beverley (first run since gelded) and others are preferred.

runners_data.name: Peel Park
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner from powerful Varian yard, poor recent form but headgear suggests improvement sought
runners_data.comment: No joy in four handicaps and he needs a transformation back in trip; blinkers added
runners_data.spotlight: Won Yarmouth maiden (6f, good to firm) last July but he's found things tough in four handicaps since; dropped another 3lb but he was beaten 11l at Ascot last month and he needs a transformation back in trip; blinkers added.

races.paceDynamic: Sanaam is the only confirmed front-runner and should get an uncontested lead at a sustainable gallop. The danger lies in the mid-race congestion with five prominent racers (King's Cavalry, Toastmaster, Rogue Messiah, King's Trust, French Affair) all wanting prime positions behind Sanaam, creating inevitable traffic problems approaching the 2f marker. The hold-up horses (Blakefell, Valpovo, Illy's Roo, Thunder Call, Peel Park) will find themselves with plenty to do as the prominent brigade bunches up ahead of them. This race shape strongly favours the front-runner Sanaam and any hold-up horse with a strong finishing kick who can navigate the traffic.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sanaam Gets Away
scenarios.trigger: If Sanaam establishes a clear lead without early pressure from the prominent pack
scenarios.body: The uncontested gallop allows him to dictate terms and kick clear when the traffic problems develop behind, while the congested prominent runners compromise each other's chances. His tactical advantage becomes decisive as the hold-up horses have too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Hero Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent traffic creates a wall that one hold-up horse can weave through or go around
scenarios.body: Thunder Call or Blakefell with their patient tactics can time their run perfectly while the prominent brigade gets tangled up. The Haggas/Marquand combination gives Thunder Call the tactical nous to exploit the chaos.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Fight Back
scenarios.trigger: If King's Cavalry or Toastmaster can secure the ideal stalking position behind Sanaam without getting caught in traffic
scenarios.body: These two have the class and recent form to overcome the tactical disadvantage if they get clear sailing. King's Cavalry's recent Leicester win shows he has the tactical speed to respond when crowding develops.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Benefits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and multiple horses get severely hampered in the straight
scenarios.body: The race falls apart tactically and a horse like Night Patrol or Peel Park who gets a dream run can pick up the pieces. Varian's tactical acumen could see Peel Park positioned perfectly for such a scenario.

watchPoints.text: Watch for Sanaam being allowed to dictate completely uncontested fractions as the only natural leader
Watch King's Trust's pre-race behaviour given recent stalls issues and current headgear application
Watch the 3f-2f marker where five prominent runners will converge behind Sanaam creating inevitable traffic problems
Watch Thunder Call's positioning as Marquand typically excels at navigating tactical puzzles like this race presents
Watch Valpovo's fitness levels given the 223-day layoff since his French debut season

races.name: Apus Life Sciences Handicap

runners_data.name: City Of Kings
runners_data.note: One uncontested leader returning from 1144 days off the track but has proven class from Ascot maiden success
runners_data.comment: Very lightly raced 6yo but he has plenty to prove after a mammoth absence; new yard
runners_data.spotlight: Won Ascot maiden (7f, good) for Charlie Appleby in 2022 but he has been absent, gelded and sold for 140,000AED since well held in conditions event at Newmarket the following spring; this is only his fourth run but he returns after a 1,144 days off and has plenty to prove for another new yard.

runners_data.name: Canvas
runners_data.note: Front-running style but proven at this course and distance with two wins here last summer
runners_data.comment: Dual C&D winner who reappeared with a good fourth at Newmarket last month; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who won twice over C&D last summer and he defied this mark when beating 15 rivals at York last September; reappeared with a creditable fourth at Newmarket last month and he's a big player if he can build on that.

runners_data.name: Tilted Kilt
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing cheekpieces who won well on Southwell return but remains unpredictable
runners_data.comment: Reappeared with a win at Southwell (1m) but he was down the field at Ascot last month
runners_data.spotlight: Belatedly doubled his tally when beating five rivals on his Southwell reappearance (1m) in April; still looks feasibly treated but he's hard to predict and was never involved when a well-held seventh at Ascot last month.

runners_data.name: Talis Evolvere
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but disappointing on turf with only one win from 20 attempts on the surface
runners_data.comment: Five-time AW winner but he's 1-20 on turf and has been well held in his last three runs
runners_data.spotlight: Five-time AW winner but he's 1-20 on turf and has been well held over this trip in last two runs; down the list.

runners_data.name: Cavolo Nero
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer wearing blinkers first time who won twice as three-year-old and has solid recent Goodwood form
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice as a 3yo and latest was at Goodwood (1m, good); didn't shine at Haydock (10.4f) when last seen in April but that was behind a subsequent winner and he was runner-up at Kempton (1m, AW) in March; has claims if he can recapture that form and he's not ruled out back in trip; new headgear.

runners_data.name: It'sneverjustone
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who thrives on good ground with both wins coming in similar conditions
runners_data.comment: Two solid efforts this season and he looks worth another try at this trip; shortlisted
runners_data.spotlight: All of his 14 runs have been on good or slower and he won back-to-back handicaps at Ffos Las (7.3f) and Galway (7f) last summer; still 3lb higher than for last success but he's finished a creditable fourth in both runs this season and he looks worth another try at this trip; dangerous.

runners_data.name: Intrusively
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing visor who broke maiden recently and showed improvement at Nottingham last time
runners_data.comment: Back to form with eye-catching fourth at Nottingham last month; interesting contender
runners_data.spotlight: His sole win was in a maiden in August 2024 but he turned things around with a close fourth at Nottingham (8.3f, good) last month; didn't get the best of runs in that race and has claims if he can back that up.

runners_data.name: Sailthisshipalone
runners_data.note: Prominent style wearing cheekpieces and tongue-tie who won on stable debut and ran well on return
runners_data.comment: Won at Pontefract on his penultimate run and was a good fourth there latest; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Recorded his third win when scoring on stable debut at Pontefract (1m, good to soft) in April and he ran to a similar level when a creditable fourth on his return visit three weeks later; should go well again and he seems fairly versatile ground-wise; cheekpieces reapplied.

runners_data.name: Mr Mistoffelees
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer wearing cheekpieces on dangerous low mark but winless in 12 turf attempts
runners_data.comment: Both of his wins have been on AW and he's been well held in three runs this season
runners_data.spotlight: On dangerous mark but he's finished down the field in three runs this term and is now 0-12 in Flat turf events; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Cadarn
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won twice at Redcar but has been disappointing since joining Kevin Ryan
runners_data.comment: Two wins at Redcar last spring but he's been disappointing since; needs a major revival
runners_data.spotlight: Won two in a row at Redcar (1m, good to firm) last spring for George Boughey; now 2lb lower than for his last success but he's been disappointing since including for new yard this spring; this is a big drop back in grade but he reared at the start at York last time and others are more convincing.

runners_data.name: Rumba Numba
runners_data.note: Hold-up four-year-old returning from 311 days off with scope for improvement in handicaps
runners_data.comment: Unexposed filly who still has potential and needs a close look on her comeback
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed 4yo who won a Wolverhampton maiden (8.6f, AW) last May and she didn't get much luck when fourth on handicap debut at Glorious Goodwood (1m, good) last summer; now returns after 311 days off but she still has potential and is an interesting contender off the same mark as last time.

runners_data.name: Miletus
runners_data.note: Prominent runner wearing tongue-tie making debut for new trainer James Keane after four runs this year
runners_data.comment: Some creditable efforts for new yard this season and he has claims back up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win from 14 starts came in a soft-ground novice at Windsor (1m) in May 2024 when trained by Charlie Hills; four runs for new yard this year and he's finished runner-up twice, including over 7f here (good to soft) on his penultimate run; has possibilities back up in trip and it would be a positive if the forecast rain arrives; hood worn last time is removed.

runners_data.name: Bowood
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer ridden by 5lb claimer returning from 119 days off with solid all-weather form
runners_data.comment: All of his wins have been in lower grades and this is competitive on return; down the list
runners_data.spotlight: Two clearcut wins at Newcastle (1m, AW) last autumn but he wasn't at his best on Tapeta during the winter; has scored over C&D in the past but he's never won a Class 4 and this is competitive on his return; others preferred.

races.paceDynamic: City Of Kings will lead from the gates with Canvas and It'sneverjustone providing early support, but neither prominent runner has the pace to pressure the leader significantly. This creates a controlled tempo that will suit the patient hold-up horses who can finish strongly. With multiple closers including Tilted Kilt, Cavolo Nero, Intrusively and Mr Mistoffelees needing to be wound up from off the pace, the moderate early gallop sets up perfectly for horses that can produce late kicks. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can benefit from the steady pace and deliver finishing efforts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If City Of Kings leads uncontested and the pace stays moderate through the first half mile
scenarios.body: The patient hold-up horses get the perfect setup to unleash their finishing kicks in the final two furlongs. Multiple closers will be winding up simultaneously but the class horses with proven form will prevail.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Press Forward
scenarios.trigger: If Canvas or It'sneverjustone decide to challenge City Of Kings early and create a stronger tempo
scenarios.body: The increased pace stretches the field and favours horses that can sit handy and kick when the leaders weaken. Mid-race positioning becomes crucial as the early pace takes its toll.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish Develops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes crawling through halfway
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint from the three-furlong pole favouring horses with the highest cruising speed. Late positioning and jockey timing become everything in a bunched finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: City Of Kings Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If City Of Kings gets such an easy lead that no one can peg him back despite his long absence
scenarios.body: The returning gelding capitalises on his uncontested advantage to hold off all challengers. His class from winning at Ascot proves decisive despite the 1144-day layoff.

watchPoints.text: City Of Kings could steal this if the 1144-day absence doesn't tell and he gets an uncontested lead from the start
Canvas and It'sneverjustone may not provide enough early pace pressure allowing the leader an easy time of it
Cavolo Nero wearing blinkers for the first time could show improved urgency in his finishing kick
Multiple hold-up horses including Tilted Kilt, Intrusively and Mr Mistoffelees will need luck in running from crowded positions
Rumba Numba returning from 311 days off represents the Roger Varian yard which excels with returning horses

races.name: Join Us To Walk As One Handicap

runners_data.name: Mythical Phoenix
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with slow starts becoming problematic, needs to overcome 174-day break
runners_data.comment: Last solid run came when fourth in this last year; mark fine if 174-day break has helped
runners_data.spotlight: A solid run when fourth in this race (good) last year but he struggled subsequently, with slow starts also becoming a feature; handicapped to be competitive if a 174-day break has freshened him up.

runners_data.name: Photosynthesis
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good form for Chapple-Hyam, building on solid Newbury fourth last time
runners_data.comment: Solid fourth (6f, good) last time and he's respected from the same mark
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark for this stable at Newmarket in September; lively in the betting for both starts this spring and he built on a midfield finish at Newbury when fourth of ten at Ascot (again 6f, good) four weeks ago; respected from the same mark.

runners_data.name: Lord Bertie
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who prefers softer ground, encouraging return but inconsistent form
runners_data.comment: C&D winner but finished last behind Novello Lad three weeks ago
runners_data.spotlight: Eight visits to Doncaster yielded one soft-ground win over this trip in October; made an encouraging return when sixth of 19 in March but didn't back that up when last behind Novello Lad (again C&D, good to soft) three weeks ago; he's not the most uncomplicated but mark is fine if he can bounce back.

runners_data.name: Novello Lad
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner handed 8lb rise after career-best course win three weeks ago
runners_data.comment: Second C&D win last time; 8lb rise sets a task but he can never be discounted here
runners_data.spotlight: Track regular who added a second C&D win to his record on good to soft three weeks ago; handicapper handed him an 8lb rise but that looked a career best and he can never be discounted at this venue.

runners_data.name: Papa Cocktail
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid course record (3-1-2), competing off same mark as recent second
runners_data.spotlight: Exposed sprinter who wins in his turn these days but his C&D record reads 312; that latest visit was just one month ago and he competes from the same mark as when far from disgraced in midfield at York a fortnight ago; each-way contender.

runners_data.name: Bright
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner seeking first turf win since 2024 course victory, 28 days since last run
runners_data.spotlight: Both visits here came in the summer of 2024 and yielded a third followed by a win, both at 6f on good to firm; that was his last success on turf but he scored on AW three starts back and last month's return to grass from the widest stall at Chester can be ignored; not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Kats Bob
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who tends to lead, excellent course record for Ruth Carr
runners_data.comment: Tends to lead; now 2lb below last winning mark; case to be made but well held latest
runners_data.spotlight: Tends to lead; hit the ground running by winning his first four starts for Ruth Carr last year; plenty of good efforts followed including when he beat 18 others to score at York (6f, good to firm) in June; now 2lb below that last winning mark so a handicapping case to be made, but he did not sustain his effort when finishing well held at York a fortnight ago.

runners_data.name: Smart Vision
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with two course wins, showed faint signs of return to form last time
runners_data.spotlight: Versatile regards ground; six wins include two here (7f/5f) and he was second in this race last year; yet to get going this term but there was the faintest hint he might be on the way back at Chester (5f) last time and maybe the return to this trip can help; mark fine.

runners_data.name: Misunderstood
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who lost form badly in 2025, best watched after poor recent efforts
runners_data.comment: Has lost his way and best watched for now unless the market suggests otherwise
runners_data.spotlight: Group 3 win and Group 1 third in France as a 2yo but lost his form in 2025 and beat only one home in both starts for this yard last month; best watched unless the market suggests otherwise.

runners_data.name: Alondra
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner in good form, creditable effort when sharing third at course seven days ago
runners_data.comment: Dual 5f AW winner in February; 6f okay and has form on turf; not ruled out
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Wolverhampton (5f, AW) in February on just her second start for this yard and defied a penalty over that C&D four days later; creditable effort when sharing third over this trip at Southwell (AW) in April and maybe the cheekpieces backfired when fifth at Wolverhampton one week ago; that equipment is now removed and she has form on turf, so she's not ruled out.

runners_data.name: American Style
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who goes well fresh, close third off this mark on seasonal return
runners_data.comment: Heavy defeat latest but this is a drop back in grade so he's not completely dismissed
runners_data.spotlight: Goes well fresh and he scored on his seasonal/handicap debut last April; again ran well when close third off this mark on his comeback (also Ripon, 6f) this term; he didn't back it up when suffering a heavy defeat at York last time, albeit from a poor draw, but this represents a drop back in grade so he's not dismissed.

runners_data.name: Media Darling
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning from 237-day break, course winner on good ground
runners_data.spotlight: Made her debut only ten months ago and she bagged an Ayr maiden (6f, good to firm) in August on second start; couldn't defy a penalty on AW next time, while a swing at a Listed race proved beyond her when last seen; look for market interest on this handicap/seasonal debut.

runners_data.name: Tough Enough
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with hood removed showing improved form, second at Southwell last time
runners_data.spotlight: Dual turf winner who last won in August 2023; had reduced mark and regular hood removed when back to some form for second of six at Southwell (6f, AW; Alondra third) in April; could be rediscovering his level and he's not dismissed from the same mark.

runners_data.name: Kirkdale
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who is a non-runner having been pulled out twice from recent entries
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins (6f, AW) in April; totally unexposed at 6f on turf; key contender
runners_data.spotlight: Soft-ground 7f winner as a juvenile who hit form with back-to-back wins at Wolverhampton and Southwell (again 6f, AW) in April; pulled out twice from intended engagements last month but he's totally unexposed at 6f on turf and will be a key contender in the hat-trick bid if in the same mood.

runners_data.name: Betties Bay
runners_data.note: Prominent runner completing four-timer for James Owen, still progressing with top jockey
runners_data.comment: Rampant mare who completed a four-timer latest, going 4-4 for yard; impossible to ignore
runners_data.spotlight: Rampant mare who completed a four-timer when coming back from a break to score at Catterick (6f, good) last month; that made it 4-4 for this yard and she's still competitively weighted on form for her previous stable; impossible to ignore.

races.paceDynamic: Smart Vision is the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate a sustainable tempo without pressure early. Kats Bob tends to lead but may settle prominently behind Smart Vision, while Photosynthesis and American Style will track in prominent positions. The large field of hold-up horses (Lord Bertie, Novello Lad, Papa Cocktail, Bright, Misunderstood, Alondra, Media Darling, Tough Enough) will create a cavalry charge from the back as the pace quickens approaching the final furlong. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can finish fast in the sprint home.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Smart Vision sets an even tempo and the field stays bunched
scenarios.body: The large contingent of closers will have perfect conditions to unleash their finishing kicks in a bunched sprint finish. Horses with tactical pace like Papa Cocktail and Novello Lad can pick their way through and time their challenges perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent runners capitalize
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses get caught in traffic or fail to quicken
scenarios.body: The prominently-raced horses can steal a march as Smart Vision weakens, with American Style and Photosynthesis best placed to strike first. Their positioning gives them first run on the field while avoiding the scrimmaging behind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Early pace collapses
scenarios.trigger: If Smart Vision goes too slow and prominent horses take over
scenarios.body: Kats Bob or American Style may force the issue mid-race, creating a stronger gallop that suits those with tactical speed. This tempo change will stretch the field and favor horses who can quicken off a solid pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-runner holds on
scenarios.trigger: If Smart Vision gets an uncontested lead and the closers leave it too late
scenarios.body: The pace-setter can steal crucial lengths turning for home while the hold-up brigade struggle to make up ground on good ground. Smart Vision's course experience and front-running style could prove decisive if the finish lacks punch.

watchPoints.text: Smart Vision could get an uncontested lead if other prominent horses settle too far back
Traffic problems likely in straight with 14 runners and majority being hold-up horses
Novello Lad carries 8lb penalty but trainer Paul Midgley's horses often handle rises well
Lord Bertie and Misunderstood both from David O'Meara stable but shown contrasting form recently
Betties Bay's four-timer streak attracts Tom Marquand booking for James Owen yard

runners_data.name: Turtle Reef
runners_data.note: First run on turf after three all-weather efforts and 160 days off represents a significant unknown
runners_data.comment: Handicap newcomer but he's untried on turf and has something to prove on his return

runners_data.name: Battosai
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front runner with blinkers fitted, excellent recent form, and tactical advantage of uncontested lead
runners_data.spotlight: Improved form with blinkers added in his second handicap when runner-up at Salisbury (1m2f, good) 13 days ago; looks interesting off only 1lb higher here and he should make another bold bid.

runners_data.name: Aerial Silk
runners_data.note: Laboured handicap debut suggests gelding operation hasn't sparked immediate improvement for this prominent runner
runners_data.comment: Unexposed gelding but he needs improvement at this new trip
runners_data.spotlight: Reached the frame in his three 2yo runs (7f), but he returned after a gelding operation with a laboured efforts on handicap debut at Haydock (1m, good) last month; has bit to prove after that and he needs improvement at this new trip.

runners_data.name: Faeberon
runners_data.note: Clear third on handicap debut after gelding operation shows upward trajectory for this prominent type
runners_data.comment: Clear third on handicap debut at Thirsk and he's a big player on this drop back in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Big improvement after a gelding operation when a clear third on handicap debut at Thirsk (1m4f, good) last month; was only just caught in the closing stages of that race and he's just 1lb higher on this drop back in trip; big player with cheekpieces added.

runners_data.name: Filly Eilish
runners_data.note: 76 days since disappointing favourite effort but earlier promise suggests ability is there for new connections
runners_data.comment: Flopped last time but interesting to see if money arrives for her again on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Showed promise in novice events at Southwell (1m) and Wolverhampton (9.4f) in her first two starts this year; disappointing when well backed at Southwell (1m) in March but she's had wind surgery since and this well-related filly should have a future in handicaps; needs watching in market for in-form yard.

runners_data.name: Dryburgh
runners_data.note: Nine-race maiden but consistent placings when held up suggests he's found his niche with patient tactics
runners_data.comment: Two placed efforts this spring and 1m4f may have stretched him last time; not ruled out
runners_data.spotlight: Nine-race maiden, with new yard this season; upped to 1m2f, hooded and came from the rear when third at Doncaster (good to soft) and second at Nottingham (good) this spring; enters the reckoning on that form and he may have had stamina issues over 1m4f in a Class 4 at York last time; not ruled out dropped back in trip and grade.

runners_data.name: Domination
runners_data.note: Seasonal winner but disappointing follow-up suggests that Ripon success may have been his ceiling
runners_data.comment: Won at Ripon on his penultimate run and he could find more progress at this new trip
runners_data.spotlight: Justified favouritism when beating a clear second on his seasonal/stable debut at Ripon (1m, good to soft) in April; never dangerous when fourth in similar conditions at Nottingham last month but that was a Class 4 and he has shaped as though this new trip should be within range; needs a close look on this drop back in grade.

runners_data.name: Howsham
runners_data.note: Tailed off on handicap debut with history of fading in finish makes him hard to fancy despite cheekpieces
runners_data.comment: Five-race maiden and he needs a transformation with cheekpieces added back in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Well held in his four juvenile runs (6f-1m) and was tailed off at 80-1 on handicap debut at York (1m4f, good) last month; cheekpieces are now added and he needs a transformation back in trip.

runners_data.name: Madjid
runners_data.note: Course and distance second in April but failed to back it up, though hold-up style suits this race shape
runners_data.comment: Runner-up on handicap debut over C&D last month but he was only ninth at Newbury last time
runners_data.spotlight: Kicked off his handicap career with a close second over C&D (good to firm) in April but he failed to back that up when ninth of 14 at Newbury last month; still unexposed but he needs to resume his progress back at this track.

runners_data.name: Attention Seeker
runners_data.note: Regressive maiden dropping in weights but poor recent form makes him hard to recommend
runners_data.comment: Regressive nine-race maiden who was well held over 1m2f at Beverley latest; passed over
runners_data.spotlight: Regressive nine-race maiden who has form figures of 77074 in handicaps for new yard this year; continues to drop down the weights but he was well held at Beverley (1m2f) last time and others are preferred.

races.paceDynamic: Battosai is the only confirmed front runner and should be allowed to dictate a comfortable tempo early on. The real congestion comes behind him where Turtle Reef, Aerial Silk, Faeberon, Filly Eilish, Domination, and Attention Seeker all want prominent positions - creating a messy scrum 2-3 furlongs out as they jostle for racing room. This leaves the two hold-up horses Dryburgh and Madjid, plus Howsham, with cleaner runs from the rear as the pace intensifies in the final third. The uncontested leader and patient hold-up types benefit most from this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Battosai gets soft fractions and the prominent pack gets messy
scenarios.body: The lone leader kicks clear while the prominent runners impede each other in a bunched finish. Battosai's recent improvement with headgear and uncontested lead creates the perfect storm.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Profit
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion creates a strong pace and traffic problems
scenarios.body: The six horses fighting for prominent positions ensure a good gallop while blocking each other's finishing kicks. Dryburgh and Madjid get clean runs from deep to sweep up the pieces.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Escape
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent pack finds clear water before the congestion hits
scenarios.body: A prominent runner breaks free just before the traffic jam develops and holds on from the late closers. The key is positioning perfectly before the squeeze begins.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Battosai goes too slow early and the field bunches completely
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace creates a cavalry charge finish where anything can happen in a blanket finish. Form and class become secondary to racing luck.

watchPoints.text: Watch for traffic problems 2-3 furlongs out where six prominent runners will converge in limited space
Monitor Battosai's early fractions - if they go too slow the tactical advantage disappears completely
Check if Dryburgh and Madjid get the clean runs their hold-up style demands from this messy pace scenario
Turtle Reef's turf debut after 160 days could spring a surprise or prove he needs the run badly
Track whether any of the prominent pack can secure an early position without getting caught in the squeeze
